Kinetic Warehouse

One terminal. One shared index. A growing pile of cheap cells that somehow never lose track of your mountain of grit. The Kinetic Warehouse is searchable storage built from physical blocks instead of magic bags. A Warehouse Terminal owns the entire item index and opens the screen. Face connected Wooden Warehouse Cells (and later reinforced ones) only add capacity. Cells never keep private inventories of their own.

When it unlocks
You need a temporal gear, a copper funnel, copper plates, and ordinary rock grit. The grit is the real gate: produce it with a powered bronze crusher and you have officially left the hand crank era. Wooden cells craft four at a time and stay deliberately cheap, so go nuts.

Building the structure
Place the terminal first. Then slap cells against the terminal or any linked cell by full block faces. Corners do not count. Beyond that the shape is yours. Snake it along a wall, stack it into a tower, wrap it around your workshop, bury it under the floor, or build a sprawling cube that takes over half the basement. As long as every cell shares a face with the network and no second terminal tries to crash the party, the warehouse does not care what it looks like. Hover the terminal: the tooltip reports linked state, total blocks, stored items, capacity, and how many different item types you have managed to hoard.

Powering it
Add a Warehouse Drive Port anywhere on the connected structure and run a shaft into its visible socket. One powered drive port runs the whole warehouse. Each physical cell adds a very small amount of load, so upgrading to reinforced cells also makes a large warehouse easier to drive. The warehouse begins operating at 16 RPM. Gear the shaft down to 16 RPM before the Drive Port when practical: running it faster does not make storage transfers faster, but it does multiply the power demand. Without power you can still open the terminal and inspect everything, but items stay exactly where they are until the drive turns again.

Using the terminal
Right click the terminal. Search and sorting run against the terminal’s index, not by scanning every cell. Drop a carried stack anywhere over the item grid to deposit it. Left click a stored item to take one, right click to take one into an empty or compatible stack, Shift click to move a full legal stack. Shift clicking from an open inventory into the terminal deposits the same way. Drag the bottom edge if you need more rows.

Belts and filters
A Warehouse Belt Input accepts items from a belt or funnel at its visible opening. A Warehouse Belt Output places stored items onto a belt at its opening. Right click either belt port to set its own whitelist or blacklist and choose exact or fuzzy matching. A blocked belt, a full warehouse, missing power, or an unsafe structure simply pauses the transfer instead of eating the item.

Expansion and removal
Wooden cells add 1,024 items each. Reinforced cells add 4,096 in the same footprint and upgrade an existing wooden cell with one pressed band batch and two iron nails. Add cells after a reload if you like. A cell can only be removed when the remaining verified structure can still hold every stored item.
